s3-xling-001.claim: A Chinese-language question about whether protein language models alone (without homology/MSA search) can surface new protein families is decisively answered by an English bioRxiv preprint on 'singletons' (unclustered sequences) as the long tail of functional diversity; Chinese-language literature and Chinese web search do not carry this result.

s3-xling-002.claim: A Chinese methodological question about what covariance non-stationarity means in spatial transcriptomics is decisively answered by one English bioRxiv preprint that actually quantifies it (3%-50% of genes across 13 Visium datasets); the Chinese-language web only has generic spatial-transcriptomics tutorials.

s3-xling-003.claim: A Chinese proteomics question about assembling a full protein sequence from redundant de novo peptide reads without a reference is decisively answered by one English bioRxiv preprint on consensus assembly; Chinese search returns only vendor service pages and general de-novo-sequencing explainers.

s3-xling-004.claim: A Chinese interpretability question about which layer a protein language model acquires secondary-structure concepts in is decisively answered by an English bioRxiv preprint doing a high-resolution, per-family dissection of concept acquisition.

s3-xling-005.claim: A Chinese single-cell question about whether a differential-expression change reflects transcription or mRNA stability is decisively answered by one English bioRxiv preprint (scATrans) that types the mechanism from unspliced-RNA residuals with no extra experiment; Chinese sources only cover RNA-velocity basics.

s3-xling-007.claim: An English question about deriving a gated-delta-rule linear attention as an approximation of softmax attention is decisively answered by a Chinese-language derivation on kexue.fm, which shows the Taylor route lands not on plain DeltaNet but directly on Gated DeltaNet; no English write-up carries that specific derivation.

s3-xling-008.claim: An English question about a general iterative framework for approximating arbitrary matrix functions (generalizing Newton-Schulz beyond rational powers) is decisively answered by a Chinese blog post that proposes exactly such a framework; the English literature only has per-case schemes (p-th roots, hyperpower, MatRL).

s3-xling-009.claim: An English question about MoE gate normalization under loss-free load balancing (sigmoid gate vs softmax with re-normalization after top-k) is decisively answered by a Chinese blog post devoted to exactly that debate; English sources cover the balancing strategy but not the normalization-order comparison as its own subject.
